question:
A page has `

Welcome

` as the first visible heading, with no h1. Why might this confuse the document outline?
options: the outline starts with h2 instead of h1, creating an implicit h1 at the top level
h1 is required and the page is invalid without it
screen readers skip h2 if h1 is missing
the outline is unaffected, h2 as the first heading is valid
explanation: The HTML5 outline algorithm creates an implicit untitled section if the first heading is not h1; this breaks logical hierarchy for assistive tech users.

question: A page has two `<h1>` tags: one in header and one in main. Why is this problematic for SEO?
options: search engines penalize pages with multiple h1 tags
the first h1 is treated as the page title, the second confuses ranking
multiple h1s indicate missing page hierarchy to crawlers
modern search engines handle multiple h1s correctly and rank normally
explanation: While modern search engines are more forgiving, multiple h1 tags historically confused outline algorithms and hierarchy signals; best practice is one h1 per page for clarity.

question: A page skips from `<h1>` to `<h3>` with no h2 between them. A screen reader user navigates by headings. What happens?
options: the screen reader announces a missing h2 level
the outline shows h3 nested under h1 with an implied h2
navigation continues normally; h2 omission is ignored
the page structure is invalid and rendering stops
explanation: The HTML5 outline algorithm creates implicit heading levels for skipped hierarchy, so h3 becomes nested under h1, which may confuse navigation.

question: A developer uses `<h4>` for a prominent page title and `<h1>` for small component labels. Why is this backwards?
options: h1 should be the primary page title, h4 should be smaller subsections
headings are purely semantic and can be used in any order
h4 is deprecated and cannot be used for titles
css styling makes hierarchy irrelevant
explanation: Heading levels indicate semantic importance and document structure; h1 should mark the main page title, h4 should mark deeper subsections, regardless of visual size.

question:
Why might `

Page Title

` plus a visible h2 break accessibility?
options: hidden h1 is still in the outline, creating a mismatch with visible h2
display:none removes the element from the dom and outline
screen readers ignore display:none elements
visibility:hidden would work better than display:none
explanation: Even with `display:none`, the h1 exists in the DOM and outline, so screen readers see an h1-to-h2 jump while sighted users only see h2, causing confusion.

question:
A page has `

Widgets

` in the header, then later `

Widgets

` in the footer. Which is true?
options: html5 allows this; both are treated as separate page titles
search engines count both h1s and may lower ranking
the second h1 starts a new implicit section in the outline
duplicate h1 text is invalid and one must be removed
explanation: In HTML5 outline algorithm, each h1 starts a new implicit section; multiple h1s with the same text typically indicate missing structure rather than proper hierarchy.

question:
A `
` element wraps `

Title

Subtitle

`. Why might this be misunderstood?
options: hgroup suppresses h2 from the outline, treating both as a single heading unit
hgroup is deprecated and should not be used
hgroup only works if h1 comes after h2
the outline shows h1 and h2 separately regardless of hgroup
explanation: `<hgroup>` is designed to group related headings so that only the h1 enters the outline, suppressing the h2 subtitle from hierarchy navigation.

question:
A page uses `

Important Section

` inside a reusable component. When the component is embedded twice, why might the outline break?
options: the h2 is repeated, creating duplicate headings in the outline
components should only use h6 to avoid hierarchy conflicts
the outline algorithm nests the second h2 differently than the first
component headings must be dynamic based on nesting depth
explanation: Outline algorithm nesting is context-dependent; the same h2 in different parts of the page may nest at different levels, breaking consistent hierarchy.

question:
A developer marks up `

Bold Title

`. Does the strong tag affect heading semantics?
options: strong inside h1 changes the semantic level of the heading
heading semantics are unchanged; strong is just styling
strong suppresses the h1 from the outline
strong forces the heading to be treated as h2
explanation: Inline elements like `<strong>` do not change heading semantics; the heading level is determined by the h1-h6 tag, not its children.

question: Why is using a heading tag for styling (e.g., `<h6>` because it is the smallest) considered an anti-pattern?
options: heading tags must match visual size or the page is invalid
using heading for style violates semantic html; css should control size
h6 is deprecated and should never be used
screen readers announce h6 differently, confusing users
explanation: Heading semantics should reflect document structure, not visual presentation; CSS controls size, so using h1-h6 for styling alone disconnects semantics from outline.
